newsitem.title: USA: Judge OKs $90 million legal fees in Prudential case.
newsitem.headline: Judge OKs $90 million legal fees in Prudential case.

text.p: A U.S. District Court Judge Thursday approved up to $90 million in lawyers' fees in a class-action lawsuit in which Prudential Insurance Co. of America was charged with misleading policyholders.

District Court Judge Alfred Wolin granted immediate payment of $45 million to a group of attorneys involved in the suit. Wolin said the remaining $45 million will be paid once the 330,000 claims against Prudential are satisfied.
Wolin said in no case shall the attorneys' fees exceed $90 million.
Prudential Insurance spokesman Robert De Fillippo said the company has "not disputed the amount of the lawyers' fees."
Prudential Insurance has been charged with misleading policyholders over a 13-year period.
The class action suit affects 10.7 million life insurance policyholders and is expected to cost Prudential anywhere from $410 million to $2 billion.
